title: ERC-8262 provider protocol vector set
description: Shape of vectors.json. The embedded `discovery` and `evidence` documents are validated by provider-discovery.schema.json and provider-evidence.schema.json, not here.

clockSkewSeconds.description: Tolerated disagreement between clocks (SPEC.md section 10.5, Clocks).

maxListItems.description: Most entries in each discovery list: deployments, keys, sources, and claims per source.

minRevocationCheckSeconds.description: Smallest revocationCheckSeconds a discovery document may declare.

maxRevocationCheckSeconds.description: Largest revocationCheckSeconds a discovery document may declare.

maxTimestamp.description: Largest timestamp either document may carry (2^32 - 1 Unix seconds).

minUngrantedRevocationsPerAnnouncer.description: Least bound a consumer may set on the revocation records of ids it never granted on, per (trust domain, announcing party as the consumer authenticated it), never per subject wallet; revocations of ids it granted on are never bounded or dropped (SPEC.md section 10.7, Revocation bound).

follows.description: An earlier evaluation case: everything it records (expected.records) is already in this case's observation store (context.seenDiscovery / seenEvidence / seenRevoked).

evidence.description: The evidence fixture (or schema case); when context.evidenceFetch.status is not 200 it is the document the announced id names, and no document is evaluated.

trustDomainId.description: The independently controlled signing domain: the lowercase DNS host that serves this provider's discovery document and evidence endpoint. A document is authoritative only when fetched over https, without redirects, from this exact host: the consumer compares the serialized host of the URL it fetched with this value as exact ASCII. Never an IP literal: the last label starts with a letter, so no WHATWG URL parser reads the host as an IPv4 address. The host proves nothing about the attestor: the consumer's allowlist pins each trust domain to its attestorProviderId per Oracle deployment, and a host it does not list is refused.

attestorProviderId.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

credentialRoots.description: Roots the Oracle holds valid (isValidCredentialRoot) and registered to the attestor (getCredentialRoot(root).providerId).

validConfigs.description: Config hashes the Oracle holds valid: isValidConfig(configHash), read at step 23 for the configHash of a statement for the evidence's proof type (7, 8 or 9).

seenDiscovery.description: Discovery fixtures in the consumer's observation store, each with the attestorProviderId the consumer pinned its trust domain to on this deployment when it recorded it: its key revocations stay recorded under that attestor.

attestorProviderId.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

seenEvidence.description: Active evidence fixtures in the consumer's observation store.

seenRevoked.description: (trustDomainId, evidenceId) pairs the consumer recorded as revoked from a 410 or a revoked body, trustDomainId being the allowlisted host it came from.

trustDomainId.description: The independently controlled signing domain: the lowercase DNS host that serves this provider's discovery document and evidence endpoint. A document is authoritative only when fetched over https, without redirects, from this exact host: the consumer compares the serialized host of the URL it fetched with this value as exact ASCII. Never an IP literal: the last label starts with a letter, so no WHATWG URL parser reads the host as an IPv4 address. The host proves nothing about the attestor: the consumer's allowlist pins each trust domain to its attestorProviderId per Oracle deployment, and a host it does not list is refused.

evidenceId.description: Replay: an unguessable capability (at least 128 bits, base64url), unique for the provider's lifetime and never reused. A consumer validates an announced id against this rule before using it, requests exactly `https://{trustDomainId}/v1/erc8262/evidence/` followed by the id, and refuses a body whose evidenceId differs (exact comparison). It keys what it has observed by (trustDomainId, evidenceId). Re-delivery with identical immutable fields is idempotent and counts once; any differing immutable field is refused. Renewal is a new evidenceId.

statement.description: The statement the consumer requires the proof to prove (SPEC.md section 10.5, step 30), tagged with the proof type it is for: null for proof type 4 (the evidence's credentialType is the statement); for 7 the accepted jurisdiction ids and the config_hash; for 8 the risk proof_type and config_hash with, for a threshold (1), its direction (1 GT, 2 LT) and bound_lower, or for a range (2), bound_lower and bound_upper (risk_score_signed leaves the other word free in each mode); for 9 those of 7 plus the least threshold_m.

jurisdictionIds.description: The ERC-8262 jurisdiction ids the consumer accepts.
The ERC-8262 jurisdiction ids the consumer accepts.

status.description: The HTTP status; null when no HTTP response arrived (a timeout, a TLS or connection failure).
The HTTP status; null when no HTTP response arrived (a timeout, a TLS or connection failure).

announcedEvidenceId.description: The evidenceId the consumer was given (announcement or its own record). Not necessarily valid: the consumer checks it against the evidence schema's evidenceId rule before building the URL.

proof.description: The Oracle-verified proof the evidence feeds, as the consumer reads it (SPEC.md section 10.5, steps 30-31). publicInputs: the publicInputs bytes of the submitCompliance call that verified it, as 32-byte lowercase hex words in ERC-8262 order (the section 10.5 layout table); the consumer accepts them only if keccak256 of their concatenation is attestation.publicInputsHash. attestation: what getHistoricalProof(proofHash) returns (subject, proofType, publicInputsHash, expiresAt) and isAttestationRevoked(proofHash) (revoked).

expiresAt.description: Live while the consumer's clock is at or before it.

records.description: What this evaluation writes to the observation store (SPEC.md section 10.8): an insert-if-absent or atomic-maximum write counts even when the store already holds the value, and a record is null only when the evaluation writes nothing of that kind. discovery: the discovery document's updatedAt and its revoked keys (keyId and credentialSigner / signerPubkeyHash), under the attestorProviderId the allowlist pins its trust domain to, when the discovery steps pass on their own, whatever the evidence; revocation: (fetch host, announced evidenceId) from a 410 or a revoked body once steps 1-3 pass; evidence: the active evidence document once steps 1-9 pass (after a conflict the store keeps the first).

heldGrant.description: What happens to a grant the consumer holds on this evidence when this evaluation is its re-evaluation (SPEC.md section 10.7, Held grants): kept (accepted; a suspension is lifted), ended (refused at step 1-5, 18, 29 or 31), or suspended (refused at any other step: not exercised, neither ended nor revoked, until a re-evaluation accepts or the grant ends at the earlier of the evidence's and the attestation's expiresAt).

requirement.description: The multi-provider requirement (SPEC.md section 10.6): one claimType, the proof type it must feed, and the statement every member's proof must prove.

claimType.description: The claim, namespaced `<namespace>.<name>`, e.g. `kyc.individual`, `personhood.unique`. Consumers map (sourceId, claimType) to their own scoring policy; a provider never sends points, categories or tiers.

proofType.description: The ERC-8262 proof type the claim feeds: 4 (ATTESTATION, credential-root inclusion), 7 (COMPLIANCE_SIGNED), 8 (RISK_SCORE_SIGNED) or 9 (COMPLIANCE_MULTI_SIGNED).

statement.description: The statement the consumer requires the proof to prove (SPEC.md section 10.5, step 30), tagged with the proof type it is for: null for proof type 4 (the evidence's credentialType is the statement); for 7 the accepted jurisdiction ids and the config_hash; for 8 the risk proof_type and config_hash with, for a threshold (1), its direction (1 GT, 2 LT) and bound_lower, or for a range (2), bound_lower and bound_upper (risk_score_signed leaves the other word free in each mode); for 9 those of 7 plus the least threshold_m.
